title: An unbounded family of rational S-unit solutions
statement_alignment: The submission uses the standard rational S-unit interpretation of the source's S-unit equation; the source does not explicitly specify a number field. The conjectured absolute quadratic bound is false in this interpretation and in any version covering all number fields, since Q is one such field. The proof constructs finite sets of genuine nonzero rational solutions and proves that their cardinality divided by the square of the finite prime support is unbounded.
formal_scope: The Lean development defines rational S-units by reduced numerator and denominator support, proves the coprime-pair counting bound, the prime-support estimate, the injective rational construction, the definition bridge, and the negation of the uniform quadratic bound. It also proves the corresponding subgroup-generated formulation.
limitations: The formalization addresses the standard rational interpretation of S-units and finite prime supports. It does not claim a result for an unstated alternative convention, and it does not claim human endorsement, first-solution status, acceptance, award, or upstream merge.
